column1: # Defines whose target class is not a supported class (#239).
# docs/target-classes.md states the boundary the v1.0 criterion hangs off:
# "supported classes are exactly the rows of the first table below
# (Measured, with verdicts). The refusal tables and the Rust narrative are
# not supported classes, whatever verdicts their stories contain."
# The A-group is a rate over supported-class targets, so a committed define
# whose target's row is in a refusal table, and in no row of the first, is
# outside the corpus. Not because it refused, and not because its class
# lacks a verdict: a refusal row can record verdicts and still not be a
# supported class. cargo's and Bun's rows are that case — both record a FAIL
# under --observe syscalls (2026-09-16), both rows are in the refusal table,
# and no first-table row names either target or carries either class (#598).
# What would move one of these defines is its target or its class reaching
# the first table.
# watson is not an example of this rule either way: it is not a cohort
# define, so this file never held it, and its place in the denominator is
# the disagreement ADR 0025 records rather than resolves.
# These are here by class, not by revision. supersession.tsv records a
# define replaced by a later revision of the same target that is measured in
# the corpus; nothing here is in the corpus — cargo's r2 included, although
# the r2 define reaches a verdict under --observe syscalls — and count.py
# check keeps the two files from absorbing each other's rows.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   define  refusal_table_row  reason
# refusal_table_row is the Class cell of the docs/target-classes.md row
# this define's target appears under, quoted verbatim. count.py check holds
# each row to that page (#598). The define is tied to the rows that cite its
# cohort directory (spike/cohortN/<target>/…, any revision, outside HTML
# comments). Nothing in the
# first table may reach it: no first-table row citing that directory, none
# naming the same tool (a first word from the tied row's Tool cell, or the
# directory's own name), and this Class cell not a first-table Class cell.
# Outside the first table, a row citing the directory must carry this Class
# cell exactly. Not held: a first-table row naming the tool by some other
# word, and whether the refusal row is right about the target.
